Ann Pharmacother 2007; 41: 1013–17. Extrapyramidal disorders Extrapyramidal disorders are movement disorders involv- ing the brain’s motor systems outside the pyramidal tract. They are usually characterised by akinesia (a loss of move- ment) or bradykinesia (abnormal slowness of movement) accompanied by an increase in muscle tone (typified by parkinsonism, p.791); or by dyskinesias (abnormal invol- untary movements), often accompanied by a reduction in muscle tone (see below for some examples). Drug-in- duced extrapyramidal disorders are discussed under Chlor- promazine, p.971. Ballism.
